description:
You are acting as an observability engineer. To quickly assess your monitoring environment, you want to automate the extraction of unique service names from a log file. In the file /home/user/logs/dashboard_events.log, each log line is formatted as: 

[TIMESTAMP] SERVICE=<service_name> EVENT=<event_type>

You need to write a one-line shell command that reads /home/user/logs/dashboard_events.log, extracts all unique service names (the string that appears after "SERVICE=" and before " EVENT="), sorts them alphabetically, and writes the sorted list (one service name per line) to /home/user/logs/unique_services.txt.

For example, if the log file contains the lines:

[2024-05-01T12:00:00Z] SERVICE=api EVENT=restarted  
[2024-05-01T12:01:00Z] SERVICE=db EVENT=healthy  
[2024-05-01T12:02:00Z] SERVICE=api EVENT=scaling

The output in /home/user/logs/unique_services.txt should be:

api  
db

Ensure you overwrite the output file. Do not add any extra text, blank lines, or headers to the output. A log file of this type already exists; you only need to generate the file with unique service names as described.
truth:
Before the task:

/home/user/logs/dashboard_events.log contains:
[2024-05-01T12:00:00Z] SERVICE=api EVENT=restarted
[2024-05-01T12:01:00Z] SERVICE=db EVENT=healthy
[2024-05-01T12:02:00Z] SERVICE=api EVENT=scaling
[2024-05-01T12:03:00Z] SERVICE=frontend EVENT=deployed
[2024-05-01T12:04:00Z] SERVICE=db EVENT=backup

After successful task completion:

/home/user/logs/unique_services.txt contains:
api
db
frontend

No extra blank lines or headers. The file is overwritten if it exists.
